## Important findings and exact next actions

### Czechia — ctu-company-routes

Government service S70787 tells covered electronic-communications service providers to inform CTU immediately about non-compliance, its nature/causes and corrective measures. It specifies ePortal form 5, data box a9qaats, or podatelna@ctu.gov.cz with a recognised electronic signature. This is company notification, not a generic enquiry or a consumer complaint.
Source: https://portal.gov.cz/sluzby-vs/informovani-ceskeho-telekomunikacniho-uradu-ze-strany-poskytovatele-sluzeb-ze-poskytovana-sluzba-nesplnuje-pozadavky-na-pristupnost-S70787

Government service S70662 separately describes advance notification before providing a service relying on fundamental alteration/disproportionate burden. It requests description, reasons, unmet requirements and assessment date, with the same ePortal/data-box/signed-email options. It does not establish accepted reporting languages.
Source: https://portal.gov.cz/sluzby-vs/informovani-ceskeho-telekomunikacniho-uradu-ze-strany-poskytovatele-sluzeb-ze-poskytovana-sluzba-nebude-splnovat-pozadavky-na-pristupnost-S70662

Browser rendered form 5 without signing in: natural-person/sole-trader/legal-person choices, situation and attachment sections, consent choices, and data-box/email sending buttons. No fields entered, credentials used, validation or submission attempted. The government pages establish purpose; this observation only establishes visible intake, not successful delivery.
Source: https://eportal.ctu.gov.cz/form/5

Next: Queue a Czechia monitoring-row amendment limited to CTU electronic-communications company non-compliance and exemption routes; retain signature and audience distinctions. Source-fidelity and language review required before publication. Other transport and receiver-side 112 routes/languages remain unresolved.

### France — arcom-ebook-routes

Arcom specifies accessibilite.livresnumeriques@arcom.fr for operator non-compliance notifications and public e-book accessibility reports. Reading-software publishers may notify exemptions by this email at any time. E-book publishers instead use a restricted collection portal in campaigns (January/July after the initial campaigns); no working portal address or authenticated intake was observed. These are distinct purposes.
Source: https://www.arcom.fr/nous-connaitre-nos-missions/garantir-le-pluralisme-et-la-cohesion-sociale/accessibilite-du-livre

Official instructions include e-books/reading software in the public alert form. Access-to-audiovisual-service complaints are directed instead to the contact form with subject Accessibilité des programmes. Hardware complaints belong to DGCCRF. Article 47 website requirements on the same page must not be generalized to EAA e-book statements.
Source: https://www.arcom.fr/signaler-ou-alerter/probleme-accessibilite

Following Commencer rendered step 1 of 5 with a Livre numérique et logiciel de lecture service option and e-book title/publisher/acquisition fields. No login wall at this step. Nothing entered or submitted; later steps and delivery not tested.
Source: https://www.arcom.fr/signaler-ou-alerter/probleme-accessibilite/etape-1

Next: Queue a France monitoring amendment for exact sector-specific public/company routes, preserving correspondence and language Unknowns. Restricted publisher-exemption portal remains unverified. No new e-book reference page.

### France — arcom-other-law-news

Arcom's 14 October 2026 announcement concerns formal notices to Editions Menges, 3L and Oskar Editeur about PLATON file deposits under the intellectual-property code. This is other-law accessibility enforcement, not evidence of an EAA infringement or an imposed fine.
Source: https://www.arcom.fr/presse/accessibilite-des-livres-larcom-met-en-demeure-les-societes-editions-menges-3l-et-oskar-editeur-de-se-conformer-leurs-obligations-en-faveur-des-personnes-en-situation-de-handicap

The Menges decision is dated 22 July 2026 and published 14 October 2026. It cites intellectual-property code L122-5-1 and orders compliance within two months of notification. Notification date and subsequent compliance outcome were not established.
Source: https://www.arcom.fr/se-documenter/espace-juridique/decisions/decision-du-22-juillet-2026-mettant-en-demeure-la-societe-des-editions-menges

Next: Retain as other_law research/context, excluded from EAA case totals. Any public enforcement inclusion needs explicit scope review and a dated outcome source; no fine or completed remediation claim.

### Lithuania — rrt-lrtk-intake

RRT distinguishes provider-first dispute resolution from reports of possible electronic-communications accessibility violations. For the latter it links to Konsultacijos. This supports the reporting purpose, not company/exemption filing.
Source: https://rrt.lt/veiklos-sritys/elektroniniai-rysiai/paslaugu-vartotojams/paslaugu-prieinamumas

The linked page (updated 26 August 2025) displays an enquiry form and expressly says it is unsigned, not a written application, and the response is an employee opinion rather than RRT's official position. An unsigned email receives the same caveat. Do not label this as a formal signed complaint route.
Source: https://rrt.lt/veiklos-sritys/vartotoju-teisiu-apsauga/informacija-del-ginco-nagrinejimo/konsultacijos

LRTK guidance associated with decision KS-37 of 23 April 2025 states that users may complain to LRTK after attempting resolution with the audiovisual-access service provider (paragraph 35); paragraph 30 requires exemption notification but gives no specific filing destination. These are guidance/powers, not evidence of an actual investigation. Recommendations are explicitly non-binding explanatory material.
Source: https://www.rtk.lt/uploads/documents/files/teisine-informacija/20250926%20Gaires%20del%20prieinamumo.pdf

General LRTK submission instructions list in-person/post/fax, lrtk@rtk.lt and an online form. The form asks programme/broadcast details and a security code. Its suitability for all EAA access-service cases and company exemptions is not demonstrated; no CAPTCHA, form or email was submitted.
Source: https://www.rtk.lt/lt/paslaugos/informacijos-teikimas-asmenu-prasymu-skundu-ir-pranesimu-priemimas

Next: Queue a scoped clarification of RRT's accessibility-report referral with its unsigned-enquiry caveat. Review LRTK general email/post against EAA complaint scope; do not promote its programme-oriented form or generic mailbox to verified company/exemption intake. LTSA routes and 112 oversight remain unresolved.

### Spain — interim-complaint-pdf

The general disability-infringement procedure distinguishes state competence where conduct affects more than one autonomous community from regional competence. It is the interim general procedure previously linked by UTAC, not a dedicated EAA company/exemption channel.
Source: https://www.dsca.gob.es/es/derechos-sociales/discapacidad/derechos-personas-discapacidad/infracciones-y-sanciones

The linked one-page complaint model requires identification, alleged facts/evidence and signature; submission follows Law 39/2015 article 16.4 channels. Its data-protection email is not a complaint filing address. The filename indicates a 2020 model; current linkage does not prove all historic office details are current.
Source: https://www.dsca.gob.es/sites/default/files/derechos-sociales/discapacidad/docs/Modelo_denuncia_13112020.pdf

Next: Refine the already-queued UTAC interim-referral note with signed-form and territorial limits. Do not infer dedicated EAA intake, company/exemption filing or transfer general-law fine amounts to EAA claims.

### Finland — 2025-notification-statistics

Traficom's 2025 review, updated 6 March 2026, explicitly attributes over 200 deficiency notifications and 24 exemption notifications by end-2025 to the new EAA-related notification procedure. Counts are historical notifications, not fines or findings of violations.

### Italy — agid-regulation-access-recovered

AgID's 29 May 2026 article rendered in the browser. It describes a published accessibility-supervision regulation covering both Law 4/2004 and Decree 82/2022 service providers, with preliminary verification, requests for adjustments and possible later sanctions proceedings. This resolves article access, not a claim of a particular enforcement action, imposed sanction or EAA applicability of the older large-company threshold.
Source: https://www.agid.gov.it/it/notizie/accessibilita-pubblicato-il-nuovo-regolamento-agid-sulle-attivita-di-vigilanza

Browser displayed a 13-page PDF and its cover referencing Law 4/2004 article9 and Decree82/2022 articles21/24. Only cover/access was visually checked; operative provisions and deadlines remain unverified. Do not infer the whole document was read.
Source: https://www.agid.gov.it/sites/agid/files/2026-05/Regolamento_vigilanza_accessibilita.pdf

Next: Existing watcher/italy-2026-10-02-agid-reporting branch retains the older failed-access note; supplement it from this research queue rather than duplicate its reporting-platform work. Read the operative regulation before publishing procedural deadlines; no actual enforcement case established.

### Croatia — adopted-amendment-114-2026

Official Gazette NN114/2026-1371 was published 7 October 2026; the amendment was adopted 25 September. Article13 provides entry on the eighth day after publication (calculated 15 October2026). Article4 replaces Agencija za elektronicke medije with Agencija za medije in article25(2). Article2 requires Croatian for the product EU declaration of conformity, not general reporting languages or a dedicated service statement. Articles6–11 expand offence provisions and exclude public procurement from specified offences; these are powers, not imposed fines.
Source: https://narodne-novine.nn.hr/clanci/sluzbeni/2026_10_114_1371.html

Next: Queue a Croatia monitoring authority-name/legal-source correction and a separate sanctions-source update. Confirm the current agency identity/contact before changing links; review the amended offence coverage against the consolidated base law. Do not infer an actual case or Croatian-only complaint language.

The periodic-penalty request was withdrawn. This is an imposed Member-State lump sum, not a national authority fine on a business; payment itself was not verified.
Source: https://infocuria.curia.europa.eu/tabs/jurisprudence?lang=EN&logicDocId=id_317920&publishedId=C-646%2F24&searchTerm=%2522C%252D646%252F24%2522
